import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Age distribution
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']
ax1.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel('Age')
ax1.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax1.set_title('Age Distribution')

# 2. Income distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
df['Income'].dropna().hist(bins=30, color='coral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7, ax=ax2)
ax2.set_xlabel('Income')
ax2.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax2.set_title('Income Distribution')

# 3. Education levels
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
education_counts = df['Education'].value_counts()
ax3.bar(education_counts.index, education_counts.values, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Education')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')
ax3.set_title('Education Levels')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 4. Total spending by category
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_totals = df[spending_cols].sum()
colors_spending = ['#8B0000', '#FF6347', '#DC143C', '#4682B4', '#FFB6C1', '#FFD700']
ax4.bar(range(len(spending_totals)), spending_totals.values, color=colors_spending, edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax4.set_xticks(range(len(spending_totals)))
ax4.set_xticklabels(['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold'], rotation=45, ha='right')
ax4.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax4.set_title('Total Spending by Product Category')

# 5. Purchase channels comparison
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
purchase_channels = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 'NumDealsPurchases']
channel_totals = df[purchase_channels].sum()
ax5.bar(['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store', 'Deals'], channel_totals.values, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax5.set_ylabel('Total Purchases')
ax5.set_title('Purchase Channels Comparison')

# 6. Marital Status distribution
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax6.pie(marital_counts.values, labels=marital_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=sns.color_palette('pastel'))
ax6.set_title('Marital Status Distribution')

# 7. Income vs Total Spending scatter plot
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])
ax7.scatter(df_clean['Income'], df_clean['TotalSpending'], alpha=0.6, color='purple', edgecolors='black', s=50)
ax7.set_xlabel('Income')
ax7.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax7.set_title('Income vs Total Spending')

# 8. Kids at home distribution
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
df['TotalKids'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
kids_counts = df['TotalKids'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax8.bar(kids_counts.index, kids_counts.values, color='lightcoral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax8.set_xlabel('Number of Kids at Home')
ax8.set_ylabel('Count')
ax8.set_title('Distribution of Kids at Home')

# 9. Campaign acceptance rates
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
acceptance_rates = df[campaign_cols].sum()
ax9.bar(['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response'], acceptance_rates.values, color='gold', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax9.set_ylabel('Acceptance Count')
ax9.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates')
ax9.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

plt.suptitle('Customer Marketing Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
